page1.text:
"I have come in response to your summons.
Henceforth, my sword is yours, and my destiny shall be entwined with yours. And thus, our contract is formed."

page2.text:
...Right. The contract was formed.
Just as she chose him as her Master...
...so he vowed to help her.

page3.text:
The moonlight still shines brightly in the darkness.
The shed regains its former tranquility, as if to emulate the knight's appearance.
Every time I think back, I find myself murmuring her name.

page4.text:
The azure light is all but forgotten.
Her hair, like golden sand, bathed in the moonlight.

page5.text:
Years later...
During one of my naps, I find myself remembering the clash of swords from long ago.
I don't recall the correct order of things.
Memories are distant and dim, and what I felt then is back in the distant past.

page7.text:
"Which is why, should I encounter such a person, I know they are lacking something.
And if that person continued to carry on in that fashion, the only thing awaiting them would be tragedy."

page8.text: "If you say you will not fight, fine."

page9.text: "You've got it wrong, Saber. Shirou isn't insulting Servants. This isn't going anywhere so long as you don't understand that much, so I'm stepping in."

page10.text:
"That's why you'll fight even if it sounds absurd. You'll try to win even if you know you don't have a chance, and you don't care if you die in the process.
Because, and I don't really know why, in that twisted little mind of yours, other people are more important than you are yourself."

page11.text:
It really was foolish.
No one person can save others.
If I really wanted to end this battle, I knew what I had to do from the very beginning.

page12.text:
A certain man asked...
...whether I was really not going to fight, not kill, and not let anyone kill...
If I realize my mistake, I should first decide what to fix, then decide who to punish.

page14.text:
Dazed, I reached my hand out.
...But not because I wanted help.
I just thought the sky was so far away.
That was my final thought, I think.

page15.text: "...You are too stubborn to change, aren't you?"

page16.text:
"There is no need to respond, is there?
I am your blade. Who but I can be the one to help you, Shirou?"

page17.text:
She and that sword were one.
The sword in the stone that selected the king.
The brilliance of the sword that sealed her fate was also her brilliance.

page18.text:
Her soul must still be on the battlefield.
Before daybreak...
...under the indigo sky, she just stared off into the distance, letting the wind blow by.

page19.text:
A king is not human.
One cannot protect people with human emotions.

page20.text:
"Listen, Saber. A date basically means a tryst.
Shirou may be talking about going out and having fun, but what he's really getting at here is the whole 'boy trying to attract the attention of a girl he likes' thing."

page21.text:
Ah yes, that happened too.
Luckily, the sky was high and the wind was nice and cool.
That memory still lives in his heart, clear as day.

page22.text:
"I will not break my vow as a king. I have a responsibility to fulfill my duty.
King Arthur's goal is to obtain the Holy Grail. Even if that were finished, I will never go back to being Altria.
My wish remains unchanged. From the moment I drew the sword, my vow could never change."

page23.text: "I thought you of all people would understand."

page24.text: It's a scene from so many years ago.

page25.text: "Think before you take hold of that."

page27.text:
Even after seeing that future, she only gave a firm nod.
The mage asked again if that was what she wanted.

page28.text:
"I saw many people smiling.
So this cannot be a mistake."

page29.text:
She just wanted to protect everyone.
But to do so, she had to abandon her desire to protect people.
She could not protect her country as its king if she still had a human heart.

page30.text:
Even knowing this, she drew the sword.
Even knowing this, she vowed to live as a king.
No matter what happened, her mind was made up.
She abandoned her human heart.
She was willing to give that up to protect her nation.

page31.text:
Who could have known the girl would take such a noble oath?
She was determined to fight.
Come what may, and however it might end...
She still decided to fight.
Even if an inevitable, solitary doom awaited her.

page32.text:
"I said I can make a selection. I will gladly hand over the Grail to the right person.
So, to that end, I want to hear from you, Shirou Emiya."

page33.text:
What I see...
...is an all-too-familiar living hell.

page34.text:
No matter how much they begged for help, I couldn't give it.
If there was anything I could do, it would have been to put an end to it.
I could only fix the wrongness of those living dead.
I could only make the architect of that hell pay for his sins.

page35.text:
The priest said:
The truth of ten years ago. The malice that was planted into the Holy Grail.
The reality that there was no salvation anywhere.

page36.text:
A sad event. A tragic death. Misfortune that passed.
There was no way to undo any of it.
A champion of justice is someone who can only clean up a mess that's already been made. You'll never be able to save the very people you're hoping to save.

page37.text:
I couldn't look them in the eye. I wanted to run away.
Nothing could be done.
As I listened to their pleas, I knew I had no miracle to grant.
I didn't have the strength to contradict the man claiming champions of justice were just that.
I have no apparent enemy.
I've never wished for anything for myself.

page38.text:
But let's say...
If I did have a miracle at the ready...would I...

page40.text:
I face the corpses.
I grit my teeth as I refused.

page41.text:
What is lost cannot be returned.
His pained expression alone makes her heart ache.
What was it she had said?
She could not start over.
It was her duty as the king. So she refused, over and over.

page42.text:
"Ah..."
She pledged once, so long ago...
Something she swore to herself.
She would fight.
Even if she loses everything...even if everyone in the world hates her.

page43.text:
"...I was so foolish..."
An oath from a king. A promise to fight against all odds.

page44.text: "If the Holy Grail will stain me, I do not want it. I already have everything I want."

page45.text:
Yes. She has everything she needs with her now.
Her pride as a knight. Her promise as a king.
Even the precious dream that young girl once held...

page47.text:
You have my unwavering trust and respect.
These are not my words as a king...
...but as a girl who could not protect anything. And now, I shall be your sword until the very end...

page50.text:
The sun rises.
The wind starts to pick up.
A golden glimmer shines, seeming to last forever.
In it...
"There is one thing I must tell you."
I can hear the determination in her voice.

page51.text:
"Yeah, what is it?"
I try to at least sound strong.

page52.text:
She turns.
Saber looks straight at me and says, her voice clear,
"I love you, Shirou."
She...said it.

page53.text:
The wind blows over the mountaintop.
For a moment, I close my eyes, blinded by the morning sun. Then I open them again.

page54.text:
...
I don't think I was surprised.
I just had a feeling.
Our goodbye...
...was always going to be like this.

page55.text:
All I see is the wasteland.
Saber is gone, carried off by the gusting wind.
Just like when she appeared.
She left with grace, without a trace.

page56.text:
"Yeah...that's so like you."
There are no regrets in my voice.
Every memory, both of what I've lost and of what I've gained, remain in my heart. I'll keep them all there. Forever.

page57.text: I look out at the rising sun, hoping I never forget any of this, that none of it fades from my mind for a long time to come.

page58.text:
I watch the morning glow spreading over the distant land below.
It reminds me of the golden fields she'd fought on.
This is not a story that can be shared.
It is a story of a small wish...like one made on a star.

page59.text:
It was a long journey.
The time spent...the ideal that was held up...the life I tried to live...they were all probably a nuisance.
No matter how far along the road he traveled, he never got any closer to the end.
No rest, no giving up, no hesitation... His resolve was strong.
He traveled a long path.

page60.text:
His journey was long...endless.
The reason for this was quite simple.
He did not know where he had to go or what to do to find respite.
It seems he somehow failed to find the end of his journey, though that should have been decided at the outset.

page61.text:
Nothing is eternal or immortal.
No matter how prosperous or famous something might have been, the more it is used, the more it deteriorates.
This applies to everything: machines, bodies, even a person's mind.
Everything wears out.
Everything eventually fades.
Which is why, even something one did not think of as painful at first may come to change after years of repetition.

page62.text:
Your actions may be meaningful...
...but you yourself are worthless to the end.

page63.text:
Hope and disappointment present themselves together.
Noble ideals become worn-out obligations, then finally mutate into filthy obsessions.
The things that awed us, that we looked up to as children become mundane, and although we may look back, we no longer look up.
That is simply what it is to be a normal human being.
But he was no normal human.
He carefully locks away what pains him.

page64.text:
...And so his heart of iron is a testament to tin.
That is what allows him to continue his long journey.
In exchange, his sense of joy faded. But fortunately, he was not greedy. So he was happy to receive something in return only from time to time.

page65.text:
He admired beautiful things.
He traveled, seeing many people and towns.
There were beautiful things everywhere.
But he never was able to find the brilliant star he'd been forced to part with.
His journey never ended because he had no purpose.
...Because he never found what he wanted to find.

page66.text: But it was a satisfactory life.

page67.text:
It was a long dream.
The curse... the ideal... and the consequences...all weighed heavily on him.
No matter how long the slumber, there was no awakening.
There's no movement, no refusal, and no desire...just a deep, calming breath.
It is an eternal dream and slumber.

page68.text:
The king's duties have not ended.
To fulfill the prophecy, the king does not return to the time before the sword, even after death.
Time passed, the nation prospered, and people changed.
Even when people no longer wished for a noble king, the king's vow endured.
After all...
...she shouldered many lives as the price of becoming king.

page69.text:
But...
...catching a glimpse of that dream was saddening.
Scenes that peeked out from the depths of sleep...
But now, she wants to convey her feelings, to have him, now distant and walking his path alone, hear her.
Even if it means she casts aside her humanity and becomes a machine that just repeats the same thing over and over.
Even if nobody else notices his pain.
I am here, and I know your strength.

page70.text:
But her eternal oath endures.
If the past can't be changed, then that in itself is eternity.
The oath, and its resolve, now bind the king forever.
She will never allow herself to become the person she'd been before drawing the sword from the stone.
But she still wants to see him.
Even if she has to sleep for eternity....
...she still wants her voice to reach him.

page78.text:
And then...
...a long time passed between the two of them.

page79.text:
I open my eyes.
I don't know how long I walked.
I thought I'd only been passing through desolate land, but I find myself standing in a pleasant meadow after passing through a deep forest.

page80.text:
I'm not sure where I am.
How much time has passed?
How far have I gone?
Everything is so unclear.

page81.text:
...
I drop the weight I'm carrying and rest.
Ah.
I thought I would walk forever...
But it seems like my journey ends here.

page82.text:
A wide, verdant space unfolds before me.
The constraints that so heavily weighed on me are unraveled by the wind rustling through the grass.
My heart is at peace, and each step brings me back to those days.

page83.text:
"..."
The endless blue sky reminds me of a promise I made long ago, though I never spoke it aloud.
It was a youthful illusion...a wish I made as a bluff.
Because we saw the same sky and felt the same things.
If we'd kept pursuing it, I'm sure we could have made it happen.
That's what I had thought in my hometown.

page84.text:
And then...
...she awakens from a dream as well.

page85.text:
"..."
She keeps looking up at the sky and waits hopefully.
She notices that the wind has changed direction, and finds herself fighting back tears.
As she prays, she continues waiting for her visitor.
She simply says "goodbye".
Until now, she's only hoped for it, but she is so thankful for that small ray of hope.

page86.text:
My breathing accelerates.
I don't believe it. I don't know how long it's been since my breathing was so labored.
It feels like I'm back to being that inexperienced boy.
It's a ridiculous idea. I chuckle. Just because I'm more experienced doesn't make me complete.

page87.text:
Now that I think back, I can't even remember how many times I wished upon the sky.
I wanted to see her.
I wanted to see her.
If it was at all possible, I wanted to hold her in my arms once more and tell her what I'd wanted for so long.

page88.text:
Her heart races.
But she still doesn't move.
No, she can't bear the thought of ruining all his effort of walking all this way.
She wants to start running to him right away, but she'll have to wait, just as she has been.

page89.text:
But she still has concerns.
She'd questioned whether this hope...this miracle...would really be allowed to happen.
He is not the man he was then. His mind and body have been worn down, much like the affliction she felt.
This isn't the scene that had always been on their minds.
It was not an obsession...but neither was it forgotten.
They held on to the past, though it faded, day by day.

page90.text:
That's why it kept going.
Even if this were only a dream, he would still have expected this despair with a faint glimmer of hope.

page91.text:
No.
Those deceptions are over.
The hope, once remembered as only words, returns in all its vivid brightness.
Everything that had been locked away for so long stirs to wakefulness.

page92.text:
"Oh right..."
Blood courses through her tin heart once again.
The golden earth.
Her heart has finally caught up and arrived at her hometown, which is long since lost.

page93.text:
So much feeling wells up, but there's only one thing on the tip of her tongue.
How much she missed him, how long she's waited...none of that matters anymore.

page94.text:
That's right.
In the end, he could not change his way of life.
Similarly, she was never rewarded.
But...

page95.text:
There are things which came about from protecting that promise.
In the end, something precious came from surviving all this.

page96.text:
The important things are rising to the surface.
It's lucky it had all been tucked so deep in her heart.
His smile is as boyish and naïve as it was so long ago.

page97.text:
The words that emerge come out the same as they were so long ago.
It is as if the moment simply picks up where it left off.

page98.text:
"..."
Her steps are light.
Her face breaks into a wide smile.

page101.text:
He traveled in pursuit of a star.
On every journey, he saw others off.
Much was lost, and much was made.
At the end of it all lay an infinitesimally tiny morsel that cannot begin to compare to the vast span of time that's been eaten up.
It is so very dazzling.
What remains in that tiny palm is a dazzling, coalesced brilliance. It is blinding.

page102.text:
And then...
...at the end of their long journey, the two finally meet.
This is the end of his journey in search of a star.
And now begins the pair's next long tale.
At its end...
...this world will continue to turn...in much the same way that he might one day become a star to someone else.
